implementation_notes: The idiomatic answer is a route on the framework already serving traffic: with FastAPI or Starlette the path operation decorator (@app.get("/healthz")) replaces the route structure entirely, and the handler returns a plain string or a JSON status document with the status code set deliberately (response.status_code or JSONResponse(..., status_code=503)); Flask and Django are the same shape. Because ASGI handlers are asynchronous while most database and cache clients are blocking, checks that touch the network belong in a worker thread (anyio.to_thread.run_sync / run_in_executor) behind an explicit timeout, so one slow dependency cannot push the probe past the orchestrator's deadline. A registry with aggregation and caching is only needed once several checks must be reported separately.
idiom_name: FastAPI/Starlette path operation (Flask view) returning a status document
pitfalls: A blocking check inside an async handler stalls the whole event loop, so liveness and readiness fail together for reasons unrelated to the process - offload blocking checks and bound them with a timeout.
Every poll re-executes the checks: without caching, a short probe interval multiplied by the replica count becomes a steady synthetic load on the database the check is protecting.

With multiple worker processes behind one port the probe is load-balanced across workers, so a single unhealthy worker can be reported healthy (or vice versa); probe every worker, share the readiness state, or check per-worker health explicitly.
